notes: #1 and #2 are the same Merian plate; #1 (Dutch edition, vol. 2, 1661) is the cleaner copy (#2 has a fold crease through the sky). The plate was first issued in the German Topographia Galliae (1655–61), so labeled about 1660. #9 is weak: taken from high up, the cathedral is small; drop it if a blank plate is preferred. #5 is Compiègne, not Laon. #3 (Cuve Saint-Vincent, early 1890s) is a smaller second choice for P4.
